title: Classical decision classifiers: chosen on table folds, calibrated, each beside the rule on dev
request: One classifier per decision point, trained on the generated decision sets with grouped cross-validation, calibrated, each with a card: the point, the features, the training sources, the accuracy by source and the rule's accuracy beside it.
spec: A pure trainer in dclab_core: candidates chosen by out-of-fold accuracy over table-grouped folds, refitted and calibrated; dev measured beside the rule; sealed rows refused. A build command writes one card per point; the fitted models are rebuilt, not committed.
plan: Metrics first: accuracy with an abstention counted wrong, Wilson intervals, macro figures for a choice.
Choose among logistic and boosted candidates by out-of-fold accuracy, folds grouped by table.
Refit, calibrate on the same folds, measure dev beside the rule, write the card.
Leave the sealed partition unread: its figures come once from the next package's gate.

decisions.decision: The sealed figures move to 22.3; 22.2 reports dev only, and the plan's Done-when says so.
decisions.why: 22.3 reads each sealed set once under a gate written before; reading it here first would spend it without a gate.

decisions.decision: A choice point's macro interval is a bootstrap clustered by table group; each class keeps its own Wilson interval.
decisions.why: A mean of ratios has no Wilson interval, and decisions of one table are not independent.

decisions.decision: A model's version is a hash of its candidate and its training rows.
decisions.why: Shadow answers and demotion later must tell two fitted models apart.

decisions.decision: The build refuses labels other than benchmark ones.
decisions.why: A measured label comes from a state field, which must be left out of the features; that list arrives with 22.4.

change: dclab_core/decision_models.py (new; dclab-core 0.19.0, contract decision_model_card.v1 and its schema), dclab_core/contracts.py (registers it), dclab_rnd/decision_models_build.py (new), Makefile (make decision-models), .gitignore (fitted models), the six cards; tests/test_decision_models.py (new); CHANGELOG, CLAUDE.md, the plan (Done-when amended, status), the roadmap.

findings.defect: A choice point's precision and recall carried an interval borrowed from accuracy.
findings.scenario: For semantic_role the card showed macro precision 0.9531 with an interval whose upper end was 0.9498.
findings.cause: The pooled counts of a choice are accuracy's counts; their Wilson interval does not belong to a macro mean.
findings.fix: Per-class figures with their own intervals; the macro interval from a clustered bootstrap.

findings.defect: The Done-when asked for sealed figures that this package deliberately does not read.
findings.scenario: A done status would have claimed sealed precision and recall that were never measured.
findings.cause: The order (gate first, then one sealed read) was decided after the plan was written.
findings.fix: The plan's Done-when amended: dev here, sealed in 22.3.

findings.defect: A choice point had no interval at all.
findings.scenario: semantic_role's precision and recall were reported bare.
findings.cause: The borrowed interval had been removed without a replacement.
findings.fix: A bootstrap clustered by table group for the macro figures, Wilson per class.

findings.scenario: Truth a, a, b answered a, a, z gave precision 1.0; answered a, a, a gave 0.6667.
findings.cause: Classes came from the truth only, and a class never answered was dropped from the mean.
findings.fix: Classes over truth and answers; a class never answered counts precision 0, as scikit-learn's zero_division=0.

findings.defect: Nothing was calibrated although the plan says calibrated.
findings.scenario: A boosted model's raw confidence would feed abstention and what users see.
findings.cause: Calibration was measured on dev but never applied.
findings.fix: Platt scaling on the same table-grouped folds of the training rows; the error measured after it.

findings.defect: Every fitted model had the same version.
findings.scenario: Retrained on another set, a model would record the same answerer name as the old one.
findings.cause: The answerer's default version was never set.
findings.fix: The version is a hash of the candidate and the training rows, on the card too.

findings.defect: The card overstated what dev tests.
findings.scenario: Dev holds new seeds of the same bases, not new tables.
findings.cause: The limits said only that tables were generated.
findings.fix: A limit says so, and another says intervals by table group are narrow because every table plants the same kinds.

findings.defect: A fold that could not be fitted was skipped and its rows left out of out-of-fold accuracy.
findings.scenario: A table with the only rows of one value scored nothing and raised the candidate's accuracy from 0.8 to 1.0.
findings.cause: The skipped fold also left the denominator.
findings.fix: Its rows count wrong, as an abstention does.

findings.scenario: Any caller that imported dclab_core.answerers before the contracts got an import error.
findings.cause: contracts imports decision_models to register the card, which imported names from answerers while it was still loading.
findings.fix: decision_models reads answerers by module, at call time.

findings.defect: Sealed rows passed as dev rows were measured.
findings.scenario: A caller could read the sealed partition through dev before its gate.
findings.cause: Only the training rows were checked for the sealed split.
findings.fix: Sealed rows are refused in training and in dev.

findings.defect: The new card's frozen schema did not match its final shape.
findings.scenario: The gate failed: decision_model_card changed shape but kept version v1.
findings.cause: The baseline was frozen by the first schema build, before the review fixes added fields, and a baseline is never overwritten.
findings.fix: The unreleased contract's v1 baseline frozen again from its final shape.

findings.defect: Importing the decision ledger first failed on an import cycle.
findings.scenario: from dclab_core.ledger import POINTS, as a host's first import, raised an ImportError.
findings.cause: contracts imported decision_models, which imported answerers, which imported the ledger while it was loading; the import-order test covered four modules only.
findings.fix: decision_models reads answerers when first used; the test imports every dclab_core module first, each in a fresh interpreter.

measurements.name: semantic_role on dev
measurements.gate: model accuracy above the rule's on the same dev decisions (descriptive; the promotion gate is 22.3's)
measurements.result: model accuracy 0.936 [0.9201, 0.949] against the rule's 0.8351 on 1110 dev decisions
limits: Dev holds new seeds of the same bases; the sealed partition is not read here.

measurements.name: leakage_suspect on dev
measurements.gate: model accuracy above the rule's on the same dev decisions (descriptive)
measurements.result: model accuracy 0.9706 [0.9597, 0.9786], recall 0.8333, against the rule's 0.9213, recall 0.5901, on 1258 dev decisions

measurements.name: is_identifier on dev
measurements.gate: model accuracy above the rule's on the same dev decisions (descriptive)
measurements.result: model accuracy 0.9905 [0.9834, 0.9945] against the rule's 1.0 on 1258 dev decisions
limits: The rule is exact on these planted kinds; the classifier trails it.

outcome: Six classifiers with their cards: on dev the classifier beats the rule for semantic_role, leakage_suspect, category_code and time, and trails it for is_identifier and group, where the rule is exact on these tables. The sealed figures come once from 22.3.
lessons: Decide when a sealed set is read before writing the package that could read it, and amend the plan to match.
A macro mean needs its own interval; borrowing accuracy's hides the classes it averages.
Registering a contract by import makes import order part of the interface: test each module imported first.
Freeze a new contract's baseline only after its review fixes: the first build makes the baseline, and a baseline is never overwritten.
An import-order test must cover every module of the package, not the ones the change touched.
risks: The tables are generated from ten bases; real tables may have kinds these never planted.
Measured labels need their fields left out before they can train a model.
